evidence.exact_quote: Optional collision guard: if output strongly identifies as a different Provider CLI, return `WrongBinary`. (ContractRef: Primitive:Provider)

items.impact: A wrong or hostile executable can satisfy the permissive version-output rule while deterministic WrongBinary signatures are absent, so Found does not prove provider identity.
items.statement: The document defines deterministic location and execution but leaves provider identity verification disabled by default, creating a security-critical false-positive state.
items.title: Provider identity is not established before execution

evidence.exact_quote: - The retired bridge does not create WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, final node manifests, or production build tasks.

items.impact: The retired bridge is explicitly prevented from regaining implementation authority, avoiding duplicate coverage and accidental work generation.
items.statement: BS-001 is tightly bounded to migration lineage and has concrete non-generation acceptance criteria.
items.title: Retired bridge authority is explicitly constrained

evidence.exact_quote: Binary/provider launcher discovery must include provider-owned setup-health metadata for active CLI-runtime routes such as Antigravity `agy`, Claude Code `claude`, and Cursor `cursor-agent` while keeping Codex, GitHub Copilot, OpenCode server, and direct coding-plan providers out of required CLI bridge discovery. `agy` discovery is version-gated and records command templates, account-root/env requirements, model-list support, prompt-output proof state, and unsupported format caveats without storing secrets.

items.impact: Builders cannot determine how `agy` enters BinaryLocateRequest, which candidate names and version command apply, or how its result and trace map into the existing Cursor/Claude-only contract and UI boundaries.
items.statement: BS-026 expands required CLI-runtime discovery to Antigravity without reconciling the prologue and BS-007 provider_cli contract that enumerate only Cursor Agent and Claude Code or supplying equivalent deterministic discovery data and acceptance oracles.
items.title: Antigravity expansion is not integrated into the locator contract

evidence.exact_quote: - BinaryLocator does not install, update, uninstall, crawl heuristically, orchestrate providers, authenticate, discover models, or own PM-managed browser runtime health.

items.impact: Clear non-goals reduce ownership drift into provider orchestration, authentication, model discovery, and browser-runtime management.
items.statement: BS-002 gives BinaryLocator a concrete Provider-owned scope and explicit negative authority boundaries.
items.title: Core BinaryLocator authority is bounded

evidence.exact_quote: - UI toolkit references use Slint 1.17.1 on Rust stable 1.96.1, reverified before implementation, and treat Iced as legacy.

items.impact: The pinned rewrite stack and required reverification prevent accidental legacy Iced or SQLite implementation choices.
items.statement: BS-003 carries exact platform decisions and an implementation-time reverification oracle.
items.title: Locked platform stack is explicit

evidence.exact_quote: - BinaryLocator references canonical owner docs rather than duplicating their contracts.

items.impact: Reference-only treatment of owner contracts and legacy anchors limits competing SSOTs.
items.statement: BS-004 explicitly preserves canonical owner routing and confines legacy code to read-only evidence.
items.title: Canonical reference routing is explicit

evidence.exact_quote: - BinaryLocator diagnostics may reference owner outcomes without encoding those seams as locator state, binary validation, or provider discovery contracts.

items.impact: Implementers know what BinaryLocator must not own but lack a falsifiable payload, correlation, or acknowledgement contract for handing results to runtime, permissions, route, GUI, and diagnostics owners.
items.statement: BS-005 routes many seams to other owners but specifies no concrete consumer list or cross-owner propagation oracle.
items.title: Cross-owner routing lacks a handoff contract

evidence.exact_quote: - BinaryLocator remains Provider-owned discovery, validation, and trace service.

items.impact: Canonical terminology and service ownership are unambiguous.
items.statement: BS-006 clearly fixes the Provider-owned discovery, validation, and trace boundary and canonical user-facing terminology.
items.title: Service and terminology boundary is explicit

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: BinaryLocateRequest is a conceptual Provider-domain contract with provider_cli and force_rescan required, and workspace_root, override_path, and env_path optional under the stated probing and cache-scope boundaries.

items.impact: Malformed, oversized, delimiter-bearing, or attacker-controlled PATH and override strings can reach filesystem and process resolution without a defined rejection or normalization oracle.
items.statement: The request names optional path-bearing inputs but does not constrain encoding, length, NULs, PATH parsing, environment-token allowlists, or trust provenance.
items.title: Path-bearing request inputs lack trust and validation rules

evidence.exact_quote: - Implementations emit full EventRecord diagnostics once persisted event writers are available while readers may accept EventEnvelopeV1 during transition.

items.impact: Different builders can switch emission at different times, duplicate diagnostics on retry, or persist sensitive candidate paths indefinitely, breaking deterministic observability and privacy.
items.statement: The EventEnvelopeV1-to-EventRecord transition has no capability signal, writer authority, idempotency key, failure behavior, redaction rule, or retention contract.
items.title: Trace persistence transition is not operationally defined

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: BinaryLocator probes Override, PATH, CommonLocations, then Launchers in that exact order, returns the first Valid hit, and resolves ties by layer, Provider-owned candidate-name order, then enumerated path order.

items.impact: Probe and tie-break precedence are directly testable and leave no ordering discretion.
items.statement: BS-009 fully fixes the layer and within-layer precedence order.
items.title: Probe precedence is deterministic

evidence.exact_quote: - Missing or invalid overrides return FoundButInvalid with OverrideMissing or OverrideInvalid and do not fall back to later layers.

items.impact: A path can be replaced between existence, validation, caching, and later execution, enabling symlink or file-swap attacks despite the fail-fast result contract.
items.statement: Override normalization does not define canonicalization across symlinks or reparse points, ownership checks, allowed file types, or TOCTOU-safe validation and execution.
items.title: Manual override validation is vulnerable to path replacement

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: The PATH probe layer performs OS-native PATH lookup for each candidate name, continues after invalid PATH hits, and proceeds to CommonLocations only when no valid PATH hit exists.

items.impact: OS-native lookup can select a user-controlled shadow binary, current-directory entry, relative PATH component, or ambiguous Windows extension without a specified trust disposition.
items.statement: BS-011 delegates to OS-native PATH lookup but does not define empty and relative PATH component handling, PATHEXT precedence, current-directory search, normalization, or trusted-location policy.
items.title: PATH lookup leaves platform trust semantics unspecified

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: CommonLocations enumerates Provider-owned official/default candidate paths in stable order, expands home paths, de-duplicates normalized absolutes with first occurrence winning, validates each candidate, and excludes legacy/pre-rewrite binary locations.

items.impact: Case, Unicode, separator, symlink, short-name, and reparse-point differences can produce platform-dependent de-duplication and allow the same file to be probed under multiple identities.
items.statement: The phrase normalized absolute path is not defined per operating system and has no executable examples for aliasing edge cases.
items.title: CommonLocations normalization is underspecified

evidence.exact_quote: - Immediate child directories are treated as opaque strings and selected by lexicographically greatest byte-order comparison.

items.impact: A corrupt or partially installed greatest entry can mask an older valid bundle, and concurrent installer mutation can make selection and validation non-repeatable.
items.statement: The launcher contract selects one greatest directory but does not say whether validation failure probes earlier versions, returns FoundButInvalid or NotFound, or retries when the versions tree changes during enumeration.
items.title: Version-bundle failure and race behavior is undefined

evidence.exact_quote: - PM transfers the matching helper with scp and verifies it using xxh3 hash comparison.

items.impact: A checksum obtained from or replaceable by the same compromised source cannot authenticate the helper; remote path or symlink manipulation can redirect writes or execution, and cleanup can delete unintended files.
items.statement: BS-014 specifies xxh3 comparison but not the trusted digest source, signed manifest, remote destination path, atomic install, permissions, symlink defense, SSH host-key posture, or cleanup authorization.
items.title: Remote helper verification does not establish authenticity

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: BinaryLocator validates candidates using the Provider-owned version command SSOT, executes the resolved path with a five-second timeout and enhanced PATH, parses versions deterministically, and applies lightweight platform permission checks while treating execution as authoritative.

items.impact: A candidate can inherit sensitive environment state, spawn descendants, or emit unbounded output before timeout, creating disclosure, resource exhaustion, and incomplete cleanup risks.
items.statement: Validation execution lacks an environment allowlist, working-directory rule, stdin disposition, stdout/stderr byte limits, process-tree ownership guarantee, privilege posture, and sandbox contract.
items.title: Version-command execution is not resource or environment bounded

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: A candidate is Valid when the version command completes within timeout and returns success or a non-empty parsed version; otherwise spawn failures, timeouts, and non-zero exits with no parsed version are Invalid, while WrongBinary collision guarding remains disabled until Provider SSOT signatures exist.

items.impact: Any executable that prints version-like text can become Valid even with a non-zero exit, while the only identity collision defense is disabled; callers may execute or display trust in the wrong binary.
items.statement: The Valid transition conflates output parseability with successful provider identity and health.
items.title: Non-zero wrong binaries can transition to Valid

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: BinaryLocator maintains per-user persistent provider_cli caches and per-workspace ephemeral Session caches, bypasses reads when force_rescan is true, fast-validates cached entries, writes through on Found(Valid), and evicts invalid or stale cache entries according to the source policy.

items.impact: Concurrent scans can overwrite newer results or resurrect evicted paths; crash-partial writes can corrupt state; durable absolute paths and fingerprints have no retention, access-control, or purge contract.
items.statement: The cache policy omits transaction boundaries, compare-and-swap/version rules, scan generations, lock behavior, write-failure recovery, retention, and privacy ownership.
items.title: Cache correctness is undefined under concurrency and crashes

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: BinaryLocator returns stable BinaryErrorCode values suitable for UI rendering, logs, and evidence bundles, preserving each named code and typical layer mapping.

items.impact: Callers cannot deterministically choose retry, remediation, severity, or user messaging, and timeout cleanup subreasons can drift outside the stable taxonomy.
items.statement: The stable code list has meanings and typical layers but no structured fields for cause, retryability, remediation, underlying OS code, redaction, or the timeout_terminated versus timeout_killed distinction defined earlier.
items.title: Stable errors lack deterministic recovery metadata

evidence.exact_quote: - Setup and Health/Doctor map Found to Installed, NotFound to Not Installed, and FoundButInvalid to Failed with BinaryErrorCode and trace details.

items.impact: Raw trace details can reveal usernames, workspace paths, environment-expanded paths, and installation topology, while Installed can misleadingly imply trusted identity despite permissive validation.
items.statement: The UI mapping has no redaction or disclosure tier for trace details, no localization/accessibility oracle for failure presentation, and no distinct state for found-but-untrusted identity.
items.title: Setup and Health mapping can leak paths and overstate trust

evidence.exact_quote: - Discovery matrix rows preserve OS, Provider CLI, supported footprint, PATH setup, expected probe layer, and expected resolved path patterns.

items.impact: The evidence gate can pass while races, malicious path entries, malformed wrappers, remote transfer loss, cache write failures, oversized output, and identity collisions remain untested.
items.statement: BS-020's matrix is footprint-oriented and its listed validators are document/index validators, not executable adversarial runtime or fault-injection oracles.
items.title: Evidence gates do not exercise adversarial runtime behavior

evidence.exact_quote: - trace includes every attempted candidate in order, including misses.

items.impact: A build can satisfy every listed functional check while failing identity safety, trace redaction, process-tree cleanup, cache races, remote helper authenticity, accessibility, and localization.
items.statement: The functional acceptance suite restates primary happy-path rules but omits the document's highest-risk negative and cross-system behaviors.
items.title: Functional checks are not sufficient for safety closure

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: BinaryLocator references Spec Lock, Crosswalk, DRY Rules, Glossary, Decision Policy, Contracts V0, storage-plan EventEnvelopeV1 compatibility, and read-only legacy behavior anchors without turning those references into local re-ownership.

items.impact: The unit clearly prevents read-only compatibility anchors from becoming competing product authority.
items.statement: BS-022 is a complete reference-authority constraint rather than an implementation contract.
items.title: Reference and legacy-anchor authority is bounded

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: BinaryLocator remains the owner doc for the behavior described by its preserved sections, while cross-doc ownership follows the ContractRefs and boundary notes already present in the original text.

items.impact: Result, trace, cache, event, Setup/Health, remote-helper, and Usage consumers can be omitted or integrated inconsistently without violating the generic owner statement.
items.statement: Despite its title, BS-023 does not enumerate callers or consumers, their required fields, handoff semantics, or integration acceptance oracles.
items.title: Owner and consumer map does not map consumers

evidence.exact_quote: - This structural unit creates no WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, final node manifests, or production build tasks.

items.impact: The PlanUnits anchor cannot be misread as product behavior or work-generation authority.
items.statement: BS-024 is explicitly structural and has a clear negative compile boundary.
items.title: PlanUnits heading is safely non-behavioral

evidence.exact_quote: BinaryLocator_Spec contains duplicate Deterministic discovery algorithm headings. Recovery is anchor cleanup only: preserve the live

items.impact: References can continue resolving ambiguously because the current text contains both headings and no exact surviving anchor or alias syntax is prescribed.
items.statement: BS-025 recognizes duplicate headings but does not identify the canonical occurrence, exact replacement text, compatibility alias representation, or automated assertion that proves references remain valid.
items.title: Duplicate-heading recovery is not executable

evidence.exact_quote: desktop_version_handshake (P0) is compiled as canonical Puppet Master intent for desktop_version_handshake: Add DesktopServerVersionHandshake and EmbeddedRuntimeLifecycle The preserved PM gap/delta is: No explicit DesktopServerVersionHandshake found The observed external-repo signal remains source-lineage evidence: OpenCode desktop/local server/session tab/version issues; recent release patches

items.impact: A P0 cross-system feature cannot be implemented consistently: builders may invent incompatible protocols, lifecycle ownership, mismatch handling, watchdog transitions, UI states, rollback, and compatibility behavior.
items.statement: BS-027 is a source-lineage proposal sentence plus two test labels, not a DesktopServerVersionHandshake or EmbeddedRuntimeLifecycle contract; it defines no participants, messages, versions, state machine, authority, timeouts, mismatch policy, recovery, compatibility window, or owner boundary with BinaryLocator.
items.title: Desktop version handshake has no implementable contract

segments.summary: Reviewed the complete canonical prologue, conceptual request/result contracts, deterministic discovery, remote helper, validation, caching, errors, UI mapping, acceptance matrix, references, and ownership text. The dominant adversarial finding is that permissive version parsing can establish Valid without provider identity.

Reviewed every migration, provider-update, authority, platform, reference, cross-owner, and terminology PlanUnit line. Existing scope boundaries are strong, but Antigravity is not reconciled with the Cursor/Claude request contract and cross-owner handoffs remain non-executable.

Reviewed all request, result/trace, ordering, Override, PATH, CommonLocations, and Launchers lines. Exact ordering is sound, while path trust, normalization, event transition, TOCTOU, and failed-latest-version behavior require contract closure.

Reviewed every remote-helper, subprocess validation, outcome, cache, error, UI, and evidence-gate line. Critical gaps exist in artifact authenticity and provider identity, with additional resource, concurrency, privacy, recovery, and negative-test omissions.

Reviewed all functional acceptance, reference, owner/consumer, structural, migration, duplicate-heading, and desktop-handshake lines. Structural non-behavior is well bounded, but the acceptance suite is incomplete, the consumer map is not concrete, anchor recovery is not executable, and the P0 handshake lacks an implementable contract.
